findings.quote: Read only the fuel line, and the greenest furnace is the fullest one. Read the reject bin too, and it is not.
findings.note: register/rhythm: the same antithetical-kicker cadence ('Read X... Read Y...'; 'not how full... it is how clean') recurs 3-4x, giving a faintly over-shaped, manufactured feel next to the more varied exposition of ELF-long exemplar host-2021-verb2-ELF-040 (Pantheon). Genre (real popular-science feature on glass recycling), concrete density (soda ash, Marholm works, ~3% per tenth of cullet, ~60% threshold, named source Rasmus Feld with direct quote) and question style (main-idea/detail/inference/attitude, paraphrase-register options) are otherwise fully authentic. Edge-of-range, not disqualifying; adjudication decides. Exemplars read: host-2021-verb2-ELF-040, host-ver2-2019-verb1-ELF-031, var-2022-1-verb1-ELF-031.

findings.quote: Because municipal glass can never be cleaned well enough to melt without flaws under any circumstances whatever.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. Option C is an extreme absolute eliminable by form, and the stem's clean-vs-municipal framing entails that the contamination rides in with the dirty glass (option B), giving a passage-blind reader with no domain knowledge a material edge. A and D remain substantive mechanisms, so not decided blind. blind_pick B.

findings.quote: Convinced: she shares Feld's certainty that there is no such thing as feeding a furnace too much recycled glass.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. Options A and C both express agreement with Feld (redundant same-direction pair) and D is an extreme dismissal; the qualified option B survives by form as the lone nuanced middle. A vs B still needs the passage. blind_pick B.

findings.quote: That the Kjelvarn pilots' first gains in reliable reckoning owed less to better instruments than to pooling many ordinary logs until their average steadied.
findings.note: The sibling stem q5's option B ('grants that the sea-clock did what no logbook could, yet credits the first real gains to the pilots' shared archive') states the writer's thesis outright, which decides the main-idea item; independently C is a single-detail option and D is absolute ('no pilot could trust it at all'). Cross-question corroboration inside the stems sheet, no passage needed.

findings.quote: Voyages that ended in wreck were seldom copied back into it, so the book quietly favoured routes and seasons that happened to be survivable.
findings.note: A is absolute ('could learn nothing useful'), D contradicts the premise the sheet itself supplies in q1's option B (pooling steadied the average), leaving C, whose survivorship-bias shape is the recognisable 'interesting limitation' answer for a methodology-aware solver. Part form, part design knowledge, so major.

findings.quote: That the pooling improved what the guild knew as a whole, while a pilot on a given night still had to trust his own reckoning.
findings.note: The stem itself supplies the distinction ('more accurate' voyage vs 'less wrong' collective estimate) and D is its paraphrase; B ('always more trustworthy') and C ('no longer made reckoning errors of any real consequence') are absolutes. A remains a defensible half-answer so the item is not decided, but the stem-to-option restatement is a genuine form tell.

findings.quote: Partly persuaded: the writer grants that the sea-clock did what no logbook could, yet credits the first real gains to the pilots' shared archive.
findings.note: Attitude set with three extremes (A 'fully endorses', C 'a myth with no real evidence', D 'without favouring either one') and one calibrated stance; the calibrated stance is the standard key shape and it also matches q1's option B. Blind-pickable without the passage.

findings.quote: Warm loading docks were shown to ruin the great majority of every operator's deliveries throughout the region across the year.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. Option D is an extreme over-generalisation ('every operator... throughout the region') and B is operationally odd (reefer doors open while driving on a motorway); both fall by form, leaving A vs C as direct opposites the passage must decide. blind_pick C.

findings.quote: Man bör varken förhärliga badhusen som en förlorad gemenskap eller avfärda dem som enbart primitiva reliker.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. Classic balanced-attitude key: A ('borde återuppföras') and C ('nostalgin saknar all grund') are extremes and D carries an odd editorial tail; B survives by form as the neither/nor middle. Edge without domain knowledge, but passage confirms. blind_pick B.

findings.quote: Var snön samlas påverkar smältvattnets kvalitet, fastän nyttan är begränsad och delvis omtvistad.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. A is the only hedged option among three overstatements — C ('största... alla sjöar'), D ('ofarligt'), and B a motive claim — so the qualified survivor is pickable by form. Distractors substantive enough that the passage still grounds it. blind_pick A.

findings.quote: Att ojämna amatöranteckningar ändå är en vetenskaplig tillgång som borde bevaras innan de går förlorade.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. Options A/B/C all diminish or redirect the amateur record's scientific value while D alone affirms it — a 3-1 semantic cluster visible from form. A blind reader leans D; the three remain substantive stances a passage grounds, so flag not kill. blind_pick D.
